patch.objective: Service control policies in AWS Organizations

sources.cite: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional (DOP-C02) exam guide: SDLC Automation 22%, Configuration Management and IaC 17%, Resilient Cloud Solutions 15%, Monitoring and Logging 15%, Incident and Event Response 14%, Security and Compliance 17%
sources.note: Domain 1 page read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17: 'This domain accounts for 22% of the exam content'; Task 1.4 skills 'Troubleshooting deployment issues' and 'Using different deployment methods (for example, blue/green, canary)'. The other domains' weights and wording are the course seed's (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/aws.ts); their pages were not re-read. (read for this round by an earlier pass on 2026-11-17)

sources.cite: AWS Certification, AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional certification page (current exam SAP-C03), and Tutorials Dojo, 'What's new with the AWS Certified Solutions Architect Professional SAP-C03'
sources.note: Both read through summarizing fetches on 2026-11-17. The AWS page links the SAP-C03 exam guide and prep plan but shows no domains. The Tutorials Dojo page lists the five SAP-C03 domains (cloud-native architecture design and implementation; security, compliance, and governance; cost-optimized architecture design; resilience, migration, and business continuity; operational excellence and automation) and says SAP-C03 became generally available on November 17, 2026. The weights (25/25/15/15/20) and the objective wording are the course seed's; the official SAP-C03 guide was not read (to verify).

sources.cite: AWS IAM User Guide, 'AWS: Denies access to AWS based on the requested Region'
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: 'Actions in the CloudFront, IAM, Route 53, and Support services should not be denied because these are popular AWS global services with a single endpoint that is physically located in the us-east-1 Region ... the requests would be denied without the NotAction element'; the example's NotAction lists cloudfront, iam, organizations, route53 and support, and the page says to extend it for other global services you use (budgets, globalaccelerator, waf ...). The page covers identity policies; that the same pattern is used in an SCP, that an SCP grants nothing and an explicit deny in an SCP overrides any allow in the account, and the CloudTrail message wording are from memory of the AWS Organizations guide (to verify).
